mainEntity.name: How much does a Ford Fiesta ST 1.5 EcoBoost engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full rebuilt or reconditioned Ford Fiesta ST 1.5 EcoBoost engine typically costs between £2,500 and £4,000, including supply and fit. Rebuilt units include upgraded performance components and a 12-month warranty. Main dealers often charge £6,500+ for the same replacement. Used engines are a budget alternative, starting from around £600.

mainEntity.name: Does the Ford Fiesta ST 1.5 EcoBoost have the wet belt problem?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Ford Fiesta ST 1.5 EcoBoost uses a hybrid setup: a timing chain for the camshafts, but a wet belt for the oil pump. Unlike the problematic 1.0 EcoBoost, the ST's cam drive is chain-driven and highly robust. However, the oil pump wet belt can still degrade over time, making preventative replacement at 60,000 miles highly recommended to avoid oil starvation.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Ford Fiesta ST 1.5 EcoBoost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, absolutely. The Ford Fiesta ST retains strong market values, typically ranging from £8,000 to £16,000. A full rebuilt engine replacement (£2,500-£4,000) represents a small fraction of the vehicle's total worth. Investing in a warrantied, reconditioned unit preserves the car's performance and resale value far better than a cheap, unverified used engine.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Ford Fiesta ST 1.5 EcoBoost engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A standard Ford Fiesta ST 1.5 EcoBoost engine swap typically takes 5 to 7 working days. This includes sourcing the correct 200 PS YZJA performance unit, nationwide delivery to your chosen specialist, and physical installation, ECU calibration, fluid top-up, and comprehensive road testing.

mainEntity.name: What trim levels use the YZJA 1.5 EcoBoost engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The YZJA 1.5 EcoBoost engine was fitted exclusively to the performance-oriented trim levels of the Ford Fiesta Mk8 (2018-2023). Compatible trims include ST-2 and ST-3. Standard trims (Zetec, Titanium, ST-Line) utilised the 1.0 EcoBoost or 1.1 Duratec engines.

historyTimeline.h2: Ford Fiesta ST 1.5 EcoBoost - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: When the Mk8 Ford Fiesta ST launched, it introduced a highly advanced 1.5-litre three-cylinder EcoBoost engine, delivering 200 PS and featuring cylinder deactivation technology to balance hot-hatch performance with everyday efficiency.

milestones.description: YZJA (200 PS) introduced in the Ford Fiesta ST Mk8, replacing the previous 1.6-litre four-cylinder unit. This "Dragon" engine features a timing chain for the camshafts but retains a wet belt (belt-in-oil) for the oil pump drive.
Minor ECU mapping refinements and emissions updates, though the core YZJA architecture and 200 PS output remained unchanged.
Final production year of the Ford Fiesta ST Mk8 before the model line was discontinued, cementing its status as a modern classic hot hatch.

commonProblems.h2: Ford Fiesta ST 1.5 EcoBoost Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Ford Fiesta ST 1.5 EcoBoost delivers exceptional performance, but its advanced three-cylinder architecture introduces specific thermal and lubrication stresses. The YZJA code dominates replacement demand for this variant. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure point, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Oil Pump Wet Belt Degradation - Why the Ford Fiesta ST 1.5 EcoBoost Requires Vigilant Maintenance
problems.rootCause: While the camshafts are driven by a robust timing chain, the oil pump is driven by a wet belt (belt-in-oil). Over time, this belt can degrade and shed debris, potentially clogging the oil pickup strainer and leading to oil starvation if not addressed preventatively.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacing the wet belt and full oil system flush before failure occurs.
repairOptions.longevity: Highly recommended at 60k miles or 6 years to avoid catastrophic oil starvation.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: Required if oil starvation has already caused bearing damage or engine seizure.

problems.recommendation: Given the high value and performance nature of the Ford Fiesta ST 1.5 EcoBoost, a professionally rebuilt engine with a new oil pump belt and updated components is the most reliable long-term solution. Do not attempt to run the vehicle if an oil pressure warning or sudden misfire occurs, as this can rapidly escalate to catastrophic failure.

problems.h4: Carbon Buildup & HPFP Wear - Secondary Ford Fiesta ST 1.5 EcoBoost Vulnerabilities
problems.rootCause: Direct fuel injection bypasses the intake valves, allowing carbon to accumulate over time. Combined with the high stresses of the cylinder deactivation system, this can lead to rough idling, misfires, and high-pressure fuel pump wear.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Walnut blasting for carbon removal and HPFP inspection/replacement.
repairOptions.longevity: Viable for restoring performance if caught before severe mechanical damage occurs.
